hints.S13_A1: A RAY OF SUNSHINE made even the most WORRIED PATIENT feel better. Ask: does sunshine feel cold, dull and distant - or does it comfort you? Match the adjective to what sunshine actually does to a person.
hints.S13_A2: The FOOD AND BLANKETS go TO THE FLOOD VICTIMS - things are being given, not removed. Ask: which phrase means to distribute things to many people, one by one? 'Took away', 'threw away' and 'hid away' all take things from them.
hints.S13_A3: The MEALS are FREE, so nothing comes back in return. Ask: which phrasal verb means to hand something over for nothing? 'Take away' removes it, 'run away' flees and 'break down' means to stop working.
hints.S13_A4: Mrs Tan spent WEEKS organising the effort, and the money for the ROOF has finally been raised. Ask: does this idiom mean ill, in trouble, or confused - or lifted with joy? Idioms must be learnt as one whole phrase.
hints.S13_A5: DESPITE HER BUSY SCHEDULE, she still visits EVERY WEEKEND. Ask: does she throw the time away, lose it, or forget it - or does she deliberately create space for it? Three of the choices say the time was not used well.
hints.S13_B1: Look past 'in our BLOCK' to the real subject: NOBODY. Words like nobody and everyone count as ONE person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the one ending in -s?
hints.S13_B2: HAS is already in the sentence, waiting for a partner. Ask: after 'has', do we use the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle? Only one of them can build a present perfect.
hints.S13_B3: The LORRY BROKE DOWN suddenly, cutting across something already under way, and the subject is plural. Ask: which form shows an action still in progress in the past, and which helper goes with a plural subject?
hints.S13_B4: THAN signals a comparison between exactly two, and 'powerful' is a long adjective. Ask: do long adjectives add -er, or take a helper word in front? The -est form belongs to three or several things.
hints.S13_B5: The second half gives the REASON she DONATED her old TOYS - she wanted to make the children happy. Ask: which joining word introduces a reason? 'So' would give a result instead, and 'although' would set up a contrast.
hints.S13_B6: The main clause runs on IS ('Helping others IS one of...'), and it is positive. Ask: does a positive statement take a positive tag or a negative one? The tag must echo the same verb, not borrow 'do' or 'does'.
hints.S13_B7: THE STUDENTS did the PAINTING with no outside help - and there are many of them. Ask: is the reflexive word here singular or plural, and is it first person or third? 'Ourself' is not even a real word.
hints.S13_B8: VOLUNTEERS is a countable plural noun - you can count them one, two, three. Ask: which word goes with things you can count, and which two belong with uncountable things like water or time? Count first, then choose.
hints.S13_C1: The verb LOVES stands right in front of the blank. Ask: after love, like or enjoy, does the next verb take 'to', or the -ing ending? LOVE + verb-ing is a fixed pattern - it never takes an infinitive.
hints.S13_C2: EVERY SATURDAY WITHOUT FAIL = a habit repeated again and again, and the subject is one person. Ask: in the simple present, what does a singular subject add to the plain verb?
hints.S13_C3: LAST MONTH puts this firmly in finished past time. Ask: is this verb regular or irregular? A regular verb simply takes the -ed ending - no vowel inside the word needs to change.
hints.S13_C4: WHILE signals a longer action already running when she HEARD the moving stories, and the subject counts as ONE person. Ask: which past form shows an action still going on - a finished simple past, or a helper plus the -ing form?
hints.S13_C5: The subject SEVERAL OTHER STUDENTS names more than one person, and they all worked at that same past moment. Ask: which helper does a plural subject need in the past continuous - the singular one, or the plural one?
hints.S13_C6: The word TO is already printed in the passage: 'it feels good to ___'. Ask: what follows 'to' in an infinitive - the bare verb, or a verb carrying an ending? Never add -ing to a verb that already has 'to' in front of it.
hints.S13_C7: Look at the verb right before the blank: WANTS. Ask: after want, hope or plan, does the next verb appear with -ing, or as an infinitive with its own little marker word in front? SARA is one person, so the -s stays on 'wants', not on the second verb.
hints.S13_C8: RIGHT NOW - she stands beside the new VOLUNTEERS at this very moment, on their FIRST DAY. Ask: which form shows an action happening as we speak, and which helper goes with a singular subject - the singular one, or the plural one?
hints.S13_D1: The students gave up EVERY SATURDAY at the OLD FOLKS' HOME and were PAID NOTHING at all. Ask: which box word means to offer your time freely, without being asked or paid? 'Donated' is about handing over money or goods.
hints.S13_D2: The clue: they were PAID NOTHING AT ALL and still gave up their own WEEKEND for other people. Ask: which box word describes putting others before yourself? The blank sits before 'act', so a noun like 'kindness' cannot fit.
hints.S13_D3: The NURSES are the ones feeling something here - they say they could never have COPED on their own. Ask: which box word describes a person who feels thankful? The word for work that is valued is wanted in blank 5, not here.
hints.S13_D4: The blank follows 'a huge', so it must name the effect that a FEW HOURS OF COMPANY can have. Ask: which box word means a strong effect on someone? 'Sympathy' is a feeling, not an effect.
hints.S13_D5: The RESIDENTS MADE CARDS to show what every single visit had meant to them. Ask: which box word describes something recognised as valuable and good? The word for how a person FEELS thankful is already used in blank 3.
hints.S13_E1: The underlined word means 'at this place', but the sentence is about the EXCITEMENT reaching your ears in the SCHOOL HALL. Ask: which spelling belongs to the ears? The two sound identical, so choose by meaning.
hints.S13_E2: Everything around it is past: the EVENT BEGAN, the students REGISTERED. Ask: is the underlined verb in the same tense as the rest of the story? It is regular and already ends in -e, so what has to be added?
hints.S13_E3: The story happened LAST SATURDAY, yet the underlined verb is in the present. Ask: what is the past form of this verb? It is irregular, so the -ed rule will not help - the whole word changes shape.
hints.S13_E4: The subject is THE TABLES - more than one. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular form of 'to be', or the plural one? Match the verb to the number of the subject, never to the nearest word.
hints.S13_E5: The SIGN-OFF sheet belongs to the organisers - several people, not one. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or does it only make a plural? Work out where the apostrophe must sit when the owners are many.
hints.S13_F1: The COMMUNITY LEADER is reporting a yes/no question. Ask three things: which little linking word must follow ASKED? Does the reported question keep question word order, or normal statement order? And what happens to 'you' and to 'did'?
hints.S13_F2: One event triggers the other: first she NOTICED, and only then did she act. Ask: which of the two came first? WHEN goes in front of the triggering event, so that clause must open the sentence.
